description: Snap a recorded GPS trace to the road network and say what it actually travelled over. Provide `shape` (2 to 2000 recorded points, oldest first) or `encoded_polyline` (the same trace as a polyline6 string) — not both — plus the `costing` it was travelled under: "auto" (default), "truck", "bicycle", "pedestrian" or "motor_scooter". Costing decides which roads the trace may match onto, so a walk matched as "auto" snaps to the carriageway rather than the footpath. Returns the matched path as `geometry_polyline6` (the snapped roads, not your raw points) with its `distance_m` and `duration_s`, then the roll-ups: `by_road_class` and `by_admin` (distance and time, longest first), `by_surface` (distance), and `toll`, `bridge` and `tunnel` totals. This is how you turn a dashcam or telematics log into a report — which country and region the driving happened in, how much of it was motorway, how much was tolled, how much was unpaved. Honesty: the roll-ups are summed per matched road segment, so they need not add up to `distance_m` exactly, and segments the map records no surface or admin area for are left out of that breakdown rather than filed under a guess — an entry in `by_admin` with null codes is exactly that, counted and not attributed. Needs the MapMap gateway (GATEWAY_URL + GATEWAY_API_KEY); there is no direct-backend fallback.

CostingKind.description:
Costing models exposed by the MCP tools (a deliberate subset of the
Valhalla costing list), serialised in snake_case exactly as Valhalla
names them.

oneOf.description:
Truck costing; honours dimensional limits and, when a `truck`
profile is supplied, ADR dangerous-goods restrictions.
Bicycle costing; tune it with a `bicycle` options object.

Pedestrian (walking) costing; tune it with a `pedestrian` options
object (lit streets, wheelchair/blind, hiking difficulty).

Motor scooter (moped) costing: like auto but prefers lower-speed
roads and may use ways closed to larger motor vehicles.

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

costing.description:
Costing model the trace was travelled under: `auto` (default),
`truck`, `bicycle`, `pedestrian` or `motor_scooter`. It decides
which roads the trace may be matched onto, so a walked trace
matched as `auto` snaps to the carriageway rather than the path.

encoded_polyline.description:
The trace as a Google encoded polyline with six digits of decimal
precision (polyline6) — the geometry `route` and `match_trace`
themselves return. Provide this or `shape`.

shape.description:
The trace as an ordered list of recorded points, oldest first.
Between 2 and 2000 points. Provide this or `encoded_polyline`.

name: match_trace

AdminAreaSummary.description: Distance and time the matched path spent in one administrative area.

country.description: Country name, or null as for `country_code`.

country_code.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, or null where the routing graph
places the segment in no admin area at all.

distance_m.description: Distance in this area in metres.

duration_s.description: Time in this area in seconds.

edge_count.description: How many matched segments fell in this area.

state.description: State/region name, or null when the graph records none.

state_code.description: State/region code, or null when the graph records none.

RoadClassSummary.description: Distance and time the matched path spent on one road class.

distance_m.description: Distance on this road class in metres.

duration_s.description: Time on this road class in seconds.

edge_count.description: How many matched segments carried this road class.

road_class.description:
The road class, as the routing graph records it: `motorway`,
`trunk`, `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `unclassified`,
`residential`, `service_other`.

SegmentSummary.description:
How much of the matched path carried one flag (toll, bridge, tunnel).
The engine reports no separate time for these, so distance and a count
are all that can honestly be given.

distance_m.description:
Distance carrying this flag in metres. Zero means none of the
matched path did.

edge_count.description: How many matched segments carried this flag.

SurfaceSummary.description: Distance the matched path spent on one road surface.

distance_m.description: Distance on this surface in metres.

edge_count.description: How many matched segments carried this surface.

surface.description:
The surface, as the routing graph records it: `paved_smooth`,
`paved`, `paved_rough`, `compacted`, `dirt`, `gravel`, `path`,
`impassable`.

bridge.description: Bridge portion of the matched path.

by_admin.description:
Distance and time by administrative area, longest first. An entry
whose codes are all null covers segments the graph could not place
in any admin area — counted honestly rather than guessed at.

by_road_class.description:
Distance and time by road class (`motorway`, `primary`,
`residential`, …), longest first.

by_surface.description:
Distance by road surface (`paved`, `paved_smooth`, `gravel`, …),
longest first. Empty when the graph records no surface for any
matched segment.

costing.description: Costing the trace was matched under.

distance_m.description: Length of the matched path in metres.

duration_s.description:
Travel time along the matched path in seconds, from the engine's
own time model.

edge_count.description: How many road segments the trace matched onto.

geometry_polyline6.description:
The matched path as a Google encoded polyline with six digits of
decimal precision (polyline6). This is the trace snapped to real
roads, not the raw input.

summary.description: One-line human summary of the match, for reading aloud.

toll.description: Tolled portion of the matched path.

tunnel.description: Tunnel portion of the matched path.
